title: SLO playbook: field notes & initiative sensemaking
content:
Purpose:
A compact, pragmatic playbook with field notes from recent cross-functional SLO experiments. Designed to help feature teams, platform, SRE and incident responders converge on operationalizable SLOs with minimum ceremony. This is intentionally opinionated — think ‘what we actually do this week’ rather than a polished policy doc.

Context / why this exists (short):
- Past SLO rollouts stalled on definitions and telemetry gaps.
- Teams want a fast path to an initial, measurable SLO and an ops-tested fallback strategy.
- We need consistent handoffs between product/feature owners and SRE when an SLO is missed.

Quick summary (one paragraph):
We run a 6–8 week activation cycle per service: discovery (2 weeks), smoke SLO (2 weeks), ops-hardening (2 weeks), and a lightweight retro + stabilization week. Aim: ship a signal-backed SLO, a minimal runbook, and a rollback/fallback policy. Prioritize low-cognitive-load observability (3 metrics + alert) and a single owner for decisions.

Field observations (raw notes):
- Feature teams prefer latency P95 for apex APIs, but user impact often correlates with token-tail latency. Need to map request types -> metric.
- Logged incidents show auto-retries hide degraded throughput; error rate SLOs need retry-aware counting.
- Alert noise from synthetic checks. Synthetic cadence must be aligned with traffic patterns (spiky endpoints require more samples).
- Canaries that exercise model variants surface degradation earlier than infra-only canaries.

SLO taxonomy (practical, for pilots):
- Tier 0 (platform-critical): availability 99.99% (route-level), owner: infra-sre, apply to control-plane, auth.
- Tier 1 (customer-facing core): success rate 99.9% + p95 latency guardrail, owner: feature-product + SRE.
- Tier 2 (non-critical or internal): 99.5% success, weekly budget, owner: feature-owner.
Notes: don’t over-index on % points; pair SLOs with an explicit error budget action (throttles, reduced quality mode).

Signal mapping (must do):
- Primary signal: request-level success (server 2xx + domain-specific validation)
- Secondary: end-to-end latency (p50/p95/p99) by request class
- Tertiary: downstream dependency health and queue depth (kafka lag, redis evictions)
- Synthetic probes: targeted to critical flows only, labelled with scenario id

Telemetry gaps to prioritize this sprint:
1) request-class dimension (chat vs. embeddings vs. admin) missing on ~30% of traces -> instrument in middleware (PR: middleware/trace-annotate#112)
2) dependency error attribution not surfaced in traces -> add top-level tags in model-serving runtime
3) retry-aware success metric (ticket: JIRA-OPS-987)

Cross-functional cadence (proposed minimal ritual):
- Weekly 30-min SLO sync: owners + SRE + product; quick check of signals and triage
- Bi-weekly smoke run: run through canary script + synthetic probes before deploy
- Incident-to-SLO postmortem alignment: every Sev2/above must include a short SLO impact section in the postmortem template

Runbook minimum (for each SLO):
- One-liner: what the SLO is and the owner
- How to observe: dashboards (link) and 3 queries (success, p95 latency, queue depth)
- Quick mitigations (ordered): 1) enable degraded-quality mode, 2) shift traffic to fallback model variant, 3) scale GPU pool (dedicated)
- Escalation: on 3 minute sustained breach -> on-call -> 30 minute ops warcall if error budget > threshold
- Decision authority: product + SRE jointly sign off on any quality reductions

Rollout pattern (safe & fast):
1) Start with a smoke SLO (broadly lax but measurable) for 2 weeks to validate signals
2) Tighten SLO once signal fidelity confirmed (another 2 weeks)
3) Add automated remediation hooks (traffic routing) behind a feature flag
4) If SLO churns > 3 violations in a week, initiate a rollback plan and a focused 2-week fix sprint

Escalation and comms template (short):
- Subject: [SLO] <service> breached: <metric> <period>
- TL;DR: what breached, current impact estimate, action taken, next steps
- Slack channel: #ops-<service>-alerts
- Pager: on-call SRE -> escalation to product lead at 30m if not resolved

Ownership matrix (practical):
- SLO owner: feature/product leader (decision authority on SLO target and rollback)
- Ops owner: service SRE (observability, runbook, on-call)
- Instrumentation: platform infra eng (middleware + runtime)
- QA: release engineering (canary + synthetic ops)

Decision heuristics (when to change an SLO):
- Change if telemetry quality increases -> tighten conservatively
- If repeated incidents expose a new failure mode, add a targeted SLO or dependency-level SLI instead of changing the higher-level SLO
- Avoid micro-tuning weekly. Changes should be gated by a 2-week observation window and a small experiment plan

Lightweight metrics dashboard (3 required panels):
1) SLO compliance over rolling 7d + calendarized error budget consumption
2) Request-class p95 by region
3) Dependency error attribution (top 5 callers)

Sample quick checklist for a new service onboarding (to be copy/pasted into PR template):
- [ ] initial SLO tier chosen and owner assigned
- [ ] success metric implemented and verified in staging
- [ ] latency histograms enabled by request class
- [ ] synthetic probe created for the critical flow
- [ ] basic runbook drafted and linked in service README
- [ ] canary script added to release pipeline

Experiments & probes we want to try (ideas):
- Micro-canary: route 0.5% traffic to a degrader that occasionally injects higher latency to test client-side tolerance
- Error budget-triggered autoscaler: temporarily relax batching to preserve tail latency
- Model-quality fallback: degrade to smaller quantized model and measure user-visible regressions (A/B)

Open questions (for next SLO sync):
- What counts as a user-visible failure for composite routes (e.g., multi-step chat flows)?
- How do we treat retries: count only final outcome or count attempts? (leaning toward final outcome but tag attempts separately)
- When should customers be notified vs internal ops? Thresholds?

Next actions (owner tags):
- @Jonah: instrument request-class header in middleware by 2026-12-22 (PR queued)
- @Priya: prototype the 3-panel dashboard and share link in next sync (due 2026-12-28)
- @Ethan: draft minimal runbook template and add to repo README (due 2027-01-04)
- @Maya: schedule cross-functional tabletop for canary failure scenarios (target: 2027-01-07)

Notes to self and future readers:
- Keep the first SLO simple. Getting an observable, owned SLO in prod is a much bigger win than optimizing the % target immediately.
- This doc is a living scratchpad — please add raw notes, failures, and one-offs here (not formal policy).

Links / references (quick):
- Confluence: SRE SLO primer (CONFLUENCE-1234)
- Jira: SLO instrumentation backlog (JIRA-OPS-987)
- Slack thread: #slo-onboarding (archived thread id linked above)

Retro snippets (from last cycle):
- What worked: lightweight syncs reduced time-to-agreement; smoke SLO caught an instrumentation bug early
- What didn’t: too many owners on initial decisions; we moved to single decision owner and ops co-signer

Appendix (templates to copy):
- Runbook short: one-liner, how to observe (3 queries), immediate mitigations (3 steps), escalation list (names/roles)
- Postmortem SLO impact blurb: include time window, breached SLO(s), estimated customer impact, follow-ups tied to fix owners

-- end of notes --
